newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour's Brown vows "iron" approach to spending.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour's Brown vows "iron" approach to spending.

text.p: Labour's economics spokesman, Gordon Brown, vowed on Friday to stick to tough cash spending limits to cut Britain's budget deficit if his party wins power.

"I will not veer from the rigorous, iron approach to public spending," Brown told BBC television when asked whether a Labour government would approve any above-inflation increases recommended by Britain's public-sector pay review bodies.

Brown accused the ruling Conservatives of trying to win the coming election by making "irresponsible public spending commitments", including a new Royal Yacht, an expanded cadet force and Prime Minister John Major's promise this morning to reform the uniform business rate for small companies.
In a subsequent interview with BBC radio, Brown said it would be irresponsible to give a considered opinion on the leaked pay recommendations until he had seen the full reports.
But he said: "We will operate within these tough cash limits. It would not be credible to do otherwise."
Brown accused the Conservatives of "playing fast and loose" with the public finances. They had presided over a doubling of the national debt and had left Labour to "pick up the mess", he said.
Brown said it would be particularly irresponsible to write blank cheques given uncertainty over the underlying state of Britain's economy and public finances.
"I believe that the inflationary position is worse than was set in the budget, and the public sector borrowing requirement could indeed be higher," Brown said.
"I've got to be responsible and credible about what's going to happen in the future. You don't get into the position of making all sorts of commitments before an election," he said.
"We are not going down this road of playing fast and loose with people's hopes," Brown added.

Pressed on whether a Labour government would agree to pay public sector pay increases in stages, something opposed by unions, Brown said: "You've got to look at the position at the time. There may be circumstances in which you don't need to stage and there may be circumstances where you have to."
